# Introduction

In this sheet we take some of the initial data, wrangle the data to have a proper
dataframe, and finally try to fit some models. Recall that each row is a participant 
to the experiment, and each participant is assigned to one of the two flows. The 
flow dictates what variant of a vignette the participants sees  (neutral or negative). 
In total a participant see four vignettes, two neutral and two negative.

What we aim to understand is whether the presence of negativity increases the priority 
score (measured as _effort_, _urgency_, or _importance_). 

Additionally we also record some information on the beliefs of practitioners towards 
the practice of annotating, and using, negativity in SATD as prioritization mechanism. 

```{r, include=F}
library(brms)
library(rethinking)

library(reshape2)
library(dagitty)
library(scales)

```

Create a set of dataframes with outcomes for each of the three constructs for each of the four vignettes. Als translate the perception score to a trinary scale. 

```{r, include=F}
precis(df_cast)



derive_perception <- function(row, output) {
  val <- row["perception_3"]
  
  if(is.na(val)) {
    return(NA)
  }
  
  if(row["perception_3"] > 3) {
    return("Agree")
  } else if(row["perception_3"] < 3) {
    return("Disagree")
  } else {
    return("Neutral")
  }
}

df_cast$perception = apply(df_cast, 1, derive_perception)
df_cast$perception_3 <- NULL

df_effort  <- melt(df_cast, id.vars = c("flow", "perception", "experience"), measure.vars = c('E1', 'E2', 'E3', 'E4'), value.name = "outcome", variable.name = "vignette")

df_effort$vignette <- as.numeric(df_effort$vignette)

df_importance  <- melt(df_cast, id.vars = c("flow", "perception", "experience"), measure.vars = c('I1', 'I2', 'I3', 'I4'), value.name = "outcome", variable.name = "vignette")

df_importance$vignette <- as.numeric(df_importance$vignette)

df_urgency <- melt(df_cast, id.vars = c("flow", "perception", "experience"), measure.vars = c('U1', 'U2', 'U3', 'U4'), value.name = "outcome", variable.name = "vignette")

df_urgency$vignette <- as.numeric(df_urgency$vignette)


outcome_dfs = list(
  list(Name='Effort', DF = df_effort),
  list(Name='Urgency', DF = df_urgency),
  list(Name='Importance', DF= df_importance)
)
```

## Translation

We translate the flows (using the flow variable) back to rediscover the values for constructed and sentiment. This is based on Table 3 in the manuscript.

```{r, include=F}

# the value 2 is used to encode that a vignette was negative, 
# while the 1 is used to encode neutral.
derive_sentiment <- function(row, output) {
  if(is.na(row["flow"])) {
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  if (row["flow"] == 1) {
    if(row["vignette"] == 1) {
      return(2)
    } 
    if(row["vignette"] == 2) {
      return(1)
    } 
    if(row["vignette"] == 3) {
      return(2)
    }
    if(row["vignette"] == 4) {
      return(1)
    }
  } else {
    if(row["vignette"] == 1) {
      return(1)
    } 
    if(row["vignette"] == 2) {
      return(2)
    } 
    if(row["vignette"] == 3) {
      return(1)
    }
    if(row["vignette"] == 4) {
      return(2)
    }
  }
}

derive_constructed <- function(row, output) {
  if(is.na(row["flow"])) {
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  if (row["flow"] == 1) {
    if(row["vignette"] == 1) {
      return(1)
    } 
    if(row["vignette"] == 2) {
      return(1)
    } 
    if(row["vignette"] == 3) {
      return(2)
    }
    if(row["vignette"] == 4) {
      return(2)
    }
  } else {
    if(row["vignette"] == 1) {
      return(2)
    } 
    if(row["vignette"] == 2) {
      return(2)
    } 
    if(row["vignette"] == 3) {
      return(1)
    }
    if(row["vignette"] == 4) {
      return(1)
    }
  }
}

code_perception <- function(row, output) {
  if(is.na(row["perception"])) {
    return(NA)
  }
  
  if(row["perception"] == "Agree") {
    return(3)
  } else if(row["perception"] == "Disagree") {
    return(1)
  } else{
    return(2)
  }
}

for(i in 1:3) {
  outcome_dfs[[i]]$DF$perception <- apply(outcome_dfs[[i]]$DF, 1, code_perception)
  outcome_dfs[[i]]$DF$is_neg <- apply(outcome_dfs[[i]]$DF, 1, derive_sentiment)
  outcome_dfs[[i]]$DF$constructed <- apply(outcome_dfs[[i]]$DF, 1, derive_constructed)
  
  outcome_dfs[[i]]$DF <- outcome_dfs[[i]]$DF[!rowSums((is.na(outcome_dfs[[i]]$DF))),]
}
```

## Models 

The below cell contains the model we test, the model is based on the dag created 
`ggdag.Rmd`. The model uses ordered logit as likelihood function (Chp. 12 Rethinking), because our dependent 
variable is an ordered categorical variable. 

Each vignette (V) has two variations, a negative one and a neutral one (N). Additionally, 
one ``half'' of the vignette is manually constructed. This is a variable 
we also record (C), and that we also include in some of the models. Because 
what if the influence of construction is greater than that of negativity?

The outcome variable is O. 

```{r}
fit_models_for_dataframe = function(df_in, do_log_lik) {
  
  dat <- list(
    O = df_in$outcome,
    V = df_in$vignette,
    N = df_in$is_neg,
    C = df_in$constructed,
    P = df_in$perception,
    E = df_in$experience
  )
  
  
  
  m_adjust_c <-ulam(
    alist(
      O ~ dordlogit(phi, cutpoints),
      phi <- sentiment[N, P] + constructed[C] + experience*E,
      matrix[2, 3]: sentiment ~ dnorm(0, 0.5),
      vector[2] : constructed ~ dnorm(0, 0.5),
      experience ~ dnorm(0, .5),
      ordered[4] : cutpoints ~ dnorm(0, 2)
    ), data=dat, chains = 4, cores = 4, log_lik = do_log_lik, iter=2000, force_compile = T, seed=20261013)
  
  models <- list(m_adjust_c = m_adjust_c)
  
  return(models)

}
```


## Sampling 

this is where it gets interesting, we sample from the model to understand what 
the actual impact is. In particular, per vignette, we sample a ton of observations, and we 
plot the contrast between the obtained outcomes. 

The below plots visualize the density plots of sampling from the best performing model. 
We sample twice per vignette, once for the negative instance, and once for the neutral instance, 
we then contrast these distributions (subtract them from each other), and we plot the 
resulting density. 


```{r}
draw_contrast_causal <- function(chosen_model, perception_val = 1, constructed = 1, use_priors = F) {


  if(use_priors) {
    priors <- extract.prior(chosen_model)
    
    Rsim_neutr <- mcreplicate(100,sim(chosen_model, data = list(P=perception_val, N=1, C=constructed, E=0), post=priors), mc.cores=4)
    Rsim_neg <- mcreplicate(100,sim(chosen_model, data = list(P=perception_val, N=2, C=constructed, E=0), post=priors), mc.cores=4)
  
  } else {
    Rsim_neutr <- mcreplicate(100,sim(chosen_model, data = list(P=perception_val, N=1, C=constructed, E=0)), mc.cores=4)
    Rsim_neg <- mcreplicate(100,sim(chosen_model, data = list(P=perception_val, N=2, C=constructed, E=0)), mc.cores=4)
  }
  # If this is greater than zero then the score of the negative vignette was larger.
  contrast <- Rsim_neg - Rsim_neutr
  
  scores <- c(Rsim_neutr, Rsim_neg)
  sent <- c(rep("Neutral", length(Rsim_neutr)), rep("Negative", length(Rsim_neg)))
  
  df_sim <- data.frame(Score=scores, Sentiment=sent)
  
  return(contrast)
}

```

# Putting it all together

This codes takes the `outcome_dfs` variable, and runs all of the code above, for each of the outcome variables. 

```{r, echo=F, message=F}


# Convert the value of evidence ratio to text using the definitions of 10.3758/s13428-018-01189-8
evid_ratio_to_text <- function(evid_ratio) {
  if(evid_ratio < 1/10) {
    return("\\textbf{Strong against}")
  }
  if(evid_ratio < 1/3) {
    return("\\textbf{Moderate against}")
  }
  if(evid_ratio < 1) {
    return("Anecdotal against")
  }
  if (evid_ratio < 3 ) {
    return("Anecdotal for")
  }
  if(evid_ratio < 10) {
    return("\\textbf{Moderate for}")
  } else {
    return("\\textbf{{Strong for}}")
  }
}

bayesplot_theme_set(theme_minimal())

hypothesis_table <- data.frame(perception=c("Agree", "No Opinion", "Disagree"))

for(i in 2) {  # DEVIATION 3: Urgency only (outcome_dfs[[2]])
  
  df_run <- outcome_dfs[[i]]$DF
  
  print(nrow(df_run))
  
  outcome_name <- outcome_dfs[[i]]$Name
  
  models <- fit_models_for_dataframe(df_run, F)
  
  chosen_model <- models$m_adjust_c
  
  #plot(precis(chosen_model, depth = 3))
  
  for(j in 1:3) {
    
    contrast <- draw_contrast_causal(chosen_model, perception_val = j, use_priors = F)
    
    write.csv(data.frame(list(contrast=c(contrast))), paste(outcome_name, " perception-", j, ".csv", sep=""), row.names = FALSE)
    
    contrast_priors <- draw_contrast_causal(chosen_model, perception_val = j, use_priors = T)
    
    write.csv(data.frame(list(contrast=c(contrast_priors))), paste("priors ", outcome_name, " perception-", j, ".csv", sep=""), row.names = FALSE)
    
  }
  
  posterior_raw <- extract.samples(chosen_model)
  
  # Only take the posteriors we are interested in. Compute the contrast between the 
  # scores for neutral sentiment and negative sentiment. A positive contrast value means that 
  # the presence of negativity results in a higher prioritization score. 
  
  df_posterior <- data.frame(
    "Disagree" = posterior_raw$sentiment[, 2, 1] - posterior_raw$sentiment[, 1, 1],
    "No Opinion" = posterior_raw$sentiment[, 2, 2] - posterior_raw$sentiment[, 1, 2],
    "Agree" = posterior_raw$sentiment[, 2, 3] - posterior_raw$sentiment[, 1, 3]
  )
  
  labels = c(
    "Disagree", 
    "No Opinion",
    "Agree"
  )
  
  if(outcome_name != "Effort") {
    labels = c()
  }
  
  plot <- mcmc_areas(df_posterior,
             prob = 0.89, # 89% intervals
              prob_outer = 0.99, # 99%
              point_est = "mean")
  
  
  plot <- (plot 
           + ggtitle(paste("Posteriors for ", outcome_name, sep="")) 
           + theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)) 
           + scale_y_discrete(labels = labels)
           + geom_vline(xintercept=c(0), linetype="dotted", color="black")
           )
  
  ggsave(paste("Posterior_", outcome_name,".eps", sep = ""),
         plot = plot,
         device = "pdf",
         width = 3.5,
         height = 7)
  
  
  
  priors <- extract.prior(chosen_model)
  
  # Only take the posteriors we are interested in. Compute the contrast between the 
  # scores for neutral sentiment and negative sentiment. A positive contrast value means that 
  # the presence of negativity results in a higher prioritization score. 
  
  df_prior <- data.frame(
    "Disagree" = priors$sentiment[, 2, 1] - priors$sentiment[, 1, 1],
    "No Opinion" = priors$sentiment[, 2, 2] - priors$sentiment[, 1, 2],
    "Agree" = priors$sentiment[, 2, 3] - priors$sentiment[, 1, 3]
  )
  
  labels = c(
    "Disagree", 
    "No Opinion",
    "Agree"
  )
  
  if(outcome_name != "Effort") {
    labels = c()
  }
  
  plot <- mcmc_areas(df_prior,
             prob = 0.89, # 89% intervals
              prob_outer = 0.99, # 99%
              point_est = "mean")
  
  
  plot <- (plot 
           + ggtitle(paste("Priors for ", outcome_name, sep="")) 
           + theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)) 
           + scale_y_discrete(labels = labels)
           + geom_vline(xintercept=c(0), linetype="dotted", color="black"))
  
  ggsave(paste("Prior_", outcome_name,".eps", sep = ""),
         plot = plot,
         device = "pdf",
         width = 3.5,
         height = 7)
  
  
  
  # After plotting the posterior we move on and plot the outcome of the `hypothesis` testing. 
  
  H_d <- hypothesis(df_posterior, "Disagree > 0")
  H_n <- hypothesis(df_posterior, "No.Opinion > 0")
  H_a <- hypothesis(df_posterior, "Agree > 0")
  
  df_hyp <- data.frame(
    hd = H_d$samples$H1,
    hn = H_n$samples$H1,
    ha = H_a$samples$H1
  )
  
  agree_text <- evid_ratio_to_text(H_a$hypothesis$Evid.Ratio)
  no_opinion_text <- evid_ratio_to_text(H_n$hypothesis$Evid.Ratio)
  disagree_text <- evid_ratio_to_text(H_d$hypothesis$Evid.Ratio)

  hypothesis_table[[outcome_name]] = c(agree_text, no_opinion_text, disagree_text)
  write.csv(data.frame(group=c("Agree","No Opinion","Disagree"), evid_ratio=c(H_a$hypothesis$Evid.Ratio, H_n$hypothesis$Evid.Ratio, H_d$hypothesis$Evid.Ratio), post_prob=c(H_a$hypothesis$Post.Prob, H_n$hypothesis$Post.Prob, H_d$hypothesis$Post.Prob)), paste("evidence ", outcome_name, ".csv", sep=""), row.names=FALSE)  # DEVIATION 4: save numeric evidence ratios
  
}

```
